title: Establish conservative upgrade path for diverse cross-encoder candidates with locale fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a cautious, observable upgrade path for replacing the current reranker with a set of higher-quality cross-encoder variants (including multilingual models) while protecting latency SLOs and user-facing quality. Background: recent evals showed up to +3.8% MRR on in-domain English queries using the cross-encoder-large-mix model, but p95 latency increases by ~70ms for 10-doc reranks. Scope: model candidate selection, per-locale gating, automated regression checks, rollout orchestration, canary sizing, and observability (cost and latency breakdown). Constraints: Must avoid >1.5% absolute drop in key quality signals (MRR/ndcg@10) per customer segment and keep p95 latency increase under +25% vs baseline. Work will include model offline evals, on-host performance profiling (batching and KV cache effects), and CI/regression automation. Candidates evaluated: cross-encoder-distill-en, cross-encoder-multilingual-large, cross-encoder-hybrid-compact, cross-encoder-quant4-fallback. Key metrics to track: MRR delta, ndcg@10, p50/p95 latency for 1/5/10 doc reranks, CPU/GPU utilization, cost-per-1000-requests. Outcome: upgrade path doc, automation for regression gates, canary runbooks, and a dashboard for pre/post comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: Automated regression suite that runs candidate models against canonical eval set and flags >1.5% MRR regression
Per-locale smoke tests that validate minimum coverage for top 20 locales before global rollout
Canary orchestration in console: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on quality or latency gate breaches
Latency SLO preserved: p95 increase <=25% compared to current reranker for 10-doc reranks
Dashboard showing token-level cost, per-request latency breakdown, and regression alerts linked to prompt sets
PR with change to runtime routing rules and gating policy merged and deployed to staging

rollout_plan: Phase 0: Offline eval and perf profiling on staging for top 6 locales (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Canary 1% of traffic for non-sensitive customers (48h) with tight monitoring
Phase 2: Expand to 5% for 72h if no quality/latency gates breached
Phase 3: 25% for 7 days with per-customer gating active
Phase 4: Full rollout and deprecate previous reranker version after 48h stability
test_plan: Add canonical eval set to CI that runs nightly for all candidate models
Synthetic latency injection tests to ensure rollback triggers on p95 breaches
Per-locale smoke tests that run against production-like datasets
End-to-end canary validation: synthetic traffic with expected ground-truth signals
notes: Trade-offs: larger multilingual models yield better global quality but increase per-request cost and p95 latency; we'll use locale gating to capture most uplift with limited cost impact.
KV caching: reranker requests benefit from prefix cache when queries share context; ensure cache keys include model variant and locale to avoid cross-contamination.

Fallback strategy: if luxury model breaches latency gate, route to compact hybrid cross-encoder (higher latency but acceptable quality) or to semantic-embedding-based approximate rerank depending on per-customer SLAs.
Follow-ups: add quota-aware routing for Dedicated customers to avoid unexpected overage costs during canaries.
